paragraphs.text: Assignment No: 5
Title: Program to Implement Doubly Linked List for Appointment System
Problem Statement:

Write a program to implement Doubly Linked List with the following operations:
a) Display free slots
b) Book appointment
c) Sort list based on time
d) Cancel appointment
e) Sort list based on time using pointer manipulation
Objectives:
To understand the concept and working of a Doubly Linked List.
To apply linked list operations for real-life applications like appointment scheduling.
To perform insertion, deletion, and sorting in a doubly linked list.
To practice pointer manipulation techniques in linked list implementation.
Outcomes:
Students will be able to implement and manipulate a doubly linked list.
Students will learn how to use linked lists for managing appointment booking systems.
Students will be able to sort data dynamically using pointer manipulation instead of array-based methods.
Software & Hardware Requirements:
Theory Concept:
A Doubly Linked List (DLL) is a type of linked list where each node contains three parts:
Data field – stores the actual information.
Pointer to previous node – points to the previous node in the list.
Pointer to next node – points to the next node in the list.
Unlike singly linked lists, DLL allows traversal in both forward and backward directions. This makes insertion, deletion, and sorting operations more efficient in certain scenarios.

In this problem, DLL is used to implement an appointment booking system where each node represents a time slot. Using pointer manipulation, appointments can be booked, canceled, displayed, and sorted based on time.
Algorithm:
1. Display Free Slots
Start from the head node.
Traverse the list and display only nodes marked as "Free".
2. Book Appointment
Input the desired time slot.
Traverse the list to find the slot.
If found and marked free → mark as booked.
Else → display "Slot not available".
3. Sort List Based on Time (Normal Method)
Use a bubble sort or selection sort logic.
Compare adjacent nodes’ data (time).
Swap data fields accordingly.
4. Cancel Appointment
Input the time slot to cancel.
Traverse the list.
If found and booked → mark as free.
Else → display "Appointment not found".
5. Sort Using Pointer Manipulation
Traverse list to compare adjacent nodes.
Instead of swapping data, adjust node links (prev and next).
Update head pointer if needed.
Mathematical Model (if applicable):

System S can be defined as:
S = {I, O, F}
I = Input (Time slot, operation choice)
O = Output (Slot booked/canceled/free, updated list)
F = Functions {Display(), Book(), Cancel(), SortData(), SortPointer()}
Conclusion / Analysis:
Successfully implemented a Doubly Linked List for appointment scheduling.
Performed basic operations: Display, Book, Cancel, Sort.
Understood how pointer manipulation makes sorting more efficient than swapping only data values.
The program demonstrates how data structures can be applied in real-world applications like appointment booking systems.
